title: phat-controller decision journal line
description: One line of <repo>/state/phat-controller-journal.jsonl. The file is append-only JSONL, one object per line. Each decision produces two lines sharing a decision_id: a decision line written BEFORE the action is attempted, then an outcome line written after. The ordering is the contract. A decision whose action then fails or is refused still leaves its decision line, because the journal records intent rather than effects. It is the input a second reviewing controller would need, and reconstructing intent from effects afterwards is not possible.

ts.description: UTC ISO8601, when this line was written.

seq.description: Monotonic per journal file: the line's own 1-based position. Two lines with the same decision_id are ordered by this, and a decision line always has the lower value.

decision_id.description: Joins a decision line to its outcome line.

repo.description: Absolute path of the repo the decision is about.

actor.description: The role identity, always 'Phat Controller <phat-controller@local>'. Not the agent: the role outlives whichever model held it.

agent.description: Decision lines only. The agent identity driving this pass, from AUTOMETTA_CONTROLLER_AGENT, when one is set.

pass_id.description: Present on both decision and outcome lines. The headless pass this line was written under, from the repo's state/.phat-controller-current-pass-id marker (or AUTOMETTA_CONTROLLER_PASS_ID). Null for a verb called by hand between passes. Every line sharing a pass_id is what pc_transcript_materialize collects into that pass's transcript, and state/phat-controller-transcripts/index.jsonl resolves the pass_id to where it landed.

verb.description: Decision lines only. The operation in scripts/phat-controller.sh being decided on.

stage_id.description: Decision lines only. Null for a decision about the repo rather than a stage.

rationale.description: Decision lines only. Why this, now.

evidence.description: Decision lines only. What was read to reach it.

expected_effect.description: Decision lines only. What should be true afterwards. A reviewing controller compares this against the outcome line.

result.description: Outcome lines only. 'refused' is a guard declining, 'held' is a verdict declining, 'failed' is the action itself going wrong, 'none' is the correct action having been none.

note.description: Outcome lines only. What actually happened.
